question: The demos/05-qemu-boot.py QEMU-Linux boot under hermit went from a sub-minute boot (GOOD) to a hard wedge / 600s timeout (BAD). WHY does the demo config (--no-rcb-time --max-timeslice disabled + the python controller's listening sockets) wedge, why does re-enabling rcb-time green it (slowly), is --no-rcb-time masking a determinism bug or is rcb-time a legitimate step-back (#151), and are scheduler decisions host-load independent (SACRED P0)?

root_cause_summary: CONFIRMED (single-variable A/B): the wedge = background state under --no-rcb-time --max-timeslice disabled (use_rcb_time()==false -> guest branch retirement adds ZERO vtime AND no PMU preemption is armed; step2d vtime-jump gated on empty run_queue with no future timed_waiter to jump to; committed clock races via the per-turn scheduler tick) [H1, necessary-not-sufficient] PLUS the trigger of a host-pollable listening socket fd (QMP + serial unix socket) whose readiness is host-timing-driven and monopolizes turns so the -icount vCPU never completes HPET calibration [H6]. Re-enabling rcb-time greens it because guest branch retirement then advances committed_time across the deadline (a legitimate ~5x-slow STEP-BACK, not masking) [H2/H3]. Scheduler DECISIONS are host-load independent (SACRED P0 passes) [H4]. The #1095 guest-clock-lag theory is KILLED for this wedge post-#1190 [H7]. Perf parity remains OPEN [H5].
